lessons.title: Practice Checkpoint Pearson Correlation
lessons.description: Implement pearson(xs, ys) for equal-length lists. Return 0 if either std is 0. The test checks that pearson([1, 1, 1], [1, 2, 3]) equals 0.0; pearson([1, 2, 3], [2, 4, 6]) equals 1.0.
learning_objectives: This step computes a whole-number correlation direction, using xs and 6.
lessons.starter_code:
import math

def pearson(xs, ys):
    # TODO
    pass
lessons.solution_code:
import math

def pearson(xs, ys):
    n = len(xs)
    mx = sum(xs) / n
    my = sum(ys) / n
    num = sum((x - mx) * (y - my) for x, y in zip(xs, ys))
    dx = math.sqrt(sum((x - mx) ** 2 for x in xs))
    dy = math.sqrt(sum((y - my) ** 2 for y in ys))
    if dx == 0 or dy == 0:
        return 0.0
    return num / (dx * dy)

source.name: Google Machine Learning Crash Course — Glossary: R-squared — square of the Pearson correlation coefficient between predictions and ground truth
